title: Agent Lifecycle Run Plan Issue Response
description: ALR-1102 Route 3 response (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:643-660): the 201 first-registration or 200 exact-key-replay response for POST .../agent-lifecycle/run-plans. Content-free: lists only expected identities/indexes and contract refs -- no raw predictions, no client content, no digest of content. `nonce` is delivered ONLY by this response: once in the original 201 and again, byte-identical, only in an exact transport-idempotent replay of that same response (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:655, :660). This is the Schema half of guard-killing mutation #5 (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:1143): `nonce` is REQUIRED here, and this document is the ONLY Part 1 response schema (of the two this story owns) that declares a `nonce` property at all -- agent_lifecycle_receipt_submit_response_schema.json is closed and has no such property, so injecting one there is rejected by additionalProperties:false (corpus case receipt_response_echoes_nonce). `state` is schema-const ISSUED: Route 3 always mints ISSUED at creation, and an exact replay reproduces the HISTORICAL issue response only -- it never reopens a sealed or expired plan (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:691), so this response's own state can never legitimately show SEALED/EXPIRED even though the general episode-state enum (Route 5) has three members.

experiment_run_ref.description: Present iff the optional request ref was accepted; exact replay returns the same optional field (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:651).

binding_ref.description: Immutable dependency snapshot used by this plan; its governance_scope_ref is minted in this same transaction but is a Route 5 bindings[] projection field, not part of this response (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:652).

expected_count.description: Equals expected_items.length and the resolved contract's own expected_count (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:653); that cross-field/cross-array-length equality is service_invalid (corpus case issue_response_count_mismatch), not schema-decidable. The beta ceiling (minimum 1 / maximum 10000, closing an all-zero universe -- corpus case issue_response_empty_universe) IS schema-decidable and stated directly here.

expected_items.description: Non-empty, strictly contiguous unique indexes from 0 (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:654). Contiguity and index/item_ref uniqueness across array entries require comparing sibling array elements by sub-field, which is service_invalid, not schema-decidable (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:971; corpus cases issue_response_noncontiguous_indexes, issue_response_duplicate_item_ref). minItems/maxItems (the beta ceiling) and each item's own closed shape ARE schema-decidable and enforced here.

nonce.description: Exactly 43 URL-safe characters: unpadded base64url of the 32-byte HMAC-SHA-256 nonce derivation output (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:655). Delivered only by this response (original 201 and its exact transport-idempotent replay); the Backend never stores or echoes it anywhere else.

expires_at.description: Later than issued_at; fixed at issue (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:657). That ordering is a cross-field arithmetic/temporal comparison and is service_invalid, not schema-decidable.

state.description: ISSUED at creation (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:658); an exact replay reproduces the historical issue response only, which was always ISSUED at the time it was minted (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:691) -- SEALED/EXPIRED never legitimately appear on this response even though the general Route 5 episode-state enum has three members.
